ruleName: Do not break anything off or bend anything out of the way
group: Do not break anything off or bend anything out of the way
imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer in the rough, next to a bush, finishing a practice swing with a snapped twig on the ground.
imageAlt: Teen boy golfer beside golf ball and broken twig on grass after a practice swing next to a bush.

imageVerification.repairPrompt: No changes needed; the image matches the prompt and scene specification well.

questions.title: What happens if you break a branch while practising your swing?
questions.question: You are getting ready to hit and make a practice swing. If you break a small branch that would have made your next shot easier, what happens?
questions.explanation: If you break off a branch or bend something growing to help your shot, even when practising your swing, you get a two-shot penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Swinging your club before you hit, to get ready.
Extra shots added to your score for breaking a rule.

questions.teachingTip: Remind kids not to break or bend anything growing on the golf course, even when practising swings near trees or bushes.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children may think there is no penalty for breaking a branch during practice swings.
They may believe a penalty only happens if you break something while making your real shot.

questions.title: Penalty for breaking off branches during a practice swing
questions.question: If you break a small branch that helps clear your shot while making a practice swing, what penalty do you get?
questions.explanation: Breaking branches or anything growing or fixed to improve your shot, including during a practice swing, results in a two stroke penalty.
